grep: no test under pcs-backend/tests/ issues two concurrent submit-approval requests (no asyncio.gather in tests/api/v1/)
findings.why_it_matters: This batch's headline concurrency fix is `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the record row in `submit_approval` and `approval_step`, and the in-code comments state it as a hard guarantee: two concurrent submits must be "一胜一拒" and two concurrent approvals must produce exactly one `APPROVAL_STEP_PASSED` audit row. Nothing in the repository verifies that. The unit suite runs on in-memory SQLite, where SQLAlchemy's SQLite dialect compiles `with_for_update()` to an empty string (no lock at all). The new test that is supposed to cover this (`test_second_submit_after_commit_is_409`) is serial by construction and its own docstring hands the PG verification to the "CI fresh-PG api-drift job" — but the only workflow in this repo (`.github/workflows/check-api-drift.yml`) runs `alembic upgrade head`, the OpenAPI export/drift check, `check_migration_idempotency.py`, one visual-renderer test file and the frontend typecheck; it never runs the backend API tests and never issues a concurrent request. The repo's own established escape hatch for this exact class of test (`# [→E2E] test_doc_no_unique_under_concurrent_issue` in `tests/api/v1/test_deliverable_issue.py:429`) is likewise a tombstone comment with no test behind it anywhere in the tree. Concrete consequence: deleting `.with_for_update()` from `load_record` leaves the entire suite green, and on a real PostgreSQL two concurrent submits would both return 200 with the second overwriting the first's frozen chain and writing a duplicate audit row — precisely the harm the code comment claims the lock prevents. A maintainer reading the comment has no way to know the guarantee is unverified.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the mechanism and stop the false delegation. (1) Add a dialect-level unit test that needs no PostgreSQL server: compile the locking SELECT against the PostgreSQL dialect and assert the emitted SQL contains `FOR UPDATE` (e.g. `assert 'FOR UPDATE' in str(select(PipingResult).where(PipingResult.pipe_id == pk).with_for_update().compile(dialect=postgresql.dialect()))`), so dropping or mistyping `.with_for_update()` fails loudly. (2) Fix the false delegation in `pcs-backend/tests/api/v1/test_record_approval_chain.py:441-446`: the comment claims "CI 的 fresh-PG api-drift job 负责那条链路", but that job's steps are `alembic upgrade head` / `export_openapi.py` / `check-api-drift.sh` / `check_migration_idempotency.py` / visual renderer tests / `npm run typecheck` — it runs no backend test at all. Replace the sentence with a pointer to the test that actually exists. (3) If a real two-connection concurrency test is wanted, model it on the isolated-schema subprocess harness already in `tests/alembic/test_p9_013_bind_default_record_matrix.py` (create a throwaway PG schema, then drive two independent sessions at the same record row and assert exactly one 200 and one 409).

provenance: 2bc2398:pcs-frontend/src/api/errors.ts:70-76 — the 403 docblock predates the batch and sat directly above describePcsError; the batch's only change to this region is the insertion of errorText (+14 lines) between the docblock and describePcsError
findings.why_it_matters: The 403 rule that errors.ts documents now belongs to a different function than the one it describes. The block that says «403 ⇒ 「无权查看：…」而不是 `HTTP_403：需要角色 [...]`» used to sit directly above `describePcsError`; this batch inserted `errorText` between that docblock and `describePcsError`, so the block now attaches to `errorText` — which does NOT implement the rule (for a 403 envelope `errorText` returns exactly `HTTP_403：需要角色 […]`, the wording the text says must never reach a user). `describePcsError`, the function that actually performs the 无权查看 rewrite, is now the only exported helper in the file with no documentation at all. The next caller choosing between the two near-identical helpers reads `errorText`'s doc, concludes the 403 handling lives there, and ships a machine-code 403 message to users — the outcome the orphaned comment says to avoid.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the 403 docblock back onto `describePcsError` (the function it documents: 403 ⇒ 「无权查看：…」 is implemented there, not in `errorText`), and give each helper a one-line «何时用哪个» note: `errorText` = 后端原文 + 无信封时返回纯 fallback; `describePcsError` = 403 ⇒ 「无权查看：…」 + 无信封时补 `HTTP_500：` 前缀. This batch inserted `errorText` between the 403 docblock and `describePcsError`, so the docblock now documents the wrong function and `describePcsError` carries no docblock at all.

findings.why_it_matters: The migration hard-codes the 20 tables that must receive the new `approval_chain_snapshot` JSONB column, and its own docstring says the list was reverse-derived from the ORM's `RecordMixin` leaves. Nothing in the repository re-derives that list, so the two can drift apart silently. The migration's own docstring admits the blind spot: "漏表 ⇒ `alembic check` 立刻报漂移（红），单测（从 metadata 建表）**不会**红". `alembic check` is a manual gate that this repo's CLAUDE.md documents as per-database, exit-code-255, and refused outright when the database is not at head — and `scripts/gate_alembic_check.py` is not invoked by the only CI workflow, so it does not run automatically either. Concrete consequence: the day someone adds a 21st `RecordMixin` table, the ORM metadata gains `approval_chain_snapshot` on it while the real database never gets the column. Unit tests stay green (they build the schema from ORM metadata), the migration's own table list stays valid (the new table simply is not in it), and the first symptom is a runtime `column ... does not exist` on every SELECT of that table — i.e. every read of that record type starts 500-ing in production while the whole test suite is still green. The one PG engine-level assertion in the roundtrip test only checks `flash_results`, so 19 of the 20 tables are unchecked even there.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `pcs-backend/tests/alembic/test_p9_014_record_approval_chain_snapshot.py`: collect every RecordMixin leaf subclass's `__tablename__` from ORM metadata and assert the set equals the migration module's `_TABLES` (naming the missing/extra table on failure); in the PG roundtrip also assert all 20 tables' `approval_chain_snapshot` column is `jsonb` and nullable (the roundtrip currently probes `flash_results` only). The migration's hardcoded 20-table tuple is a silent-drift point: adding a RecordMixin table without a matching migration entry fails nothing today.

findings.suggested_fix: Declare the field as an enum so FastAPI writes the vocabulary into the baseline and validates responses: change `DeliverableResponse.sign_status` (`pcs-backend/app/schemas/deliverable.py:47`) and `DeliverableSnapshotResponse.sign_status` (`:113`) from `str` to `DeliverableSignStatus` (`pcs-backend/app/models/enums.py:124`, 4 states DRAFT/PENDING/APPROVED/OBSOLETE); then re-roll the contract (`pcs-backend/docs/openapi.json` + `pcs-frontend/openapi.snapshot.json` + `npm run api:gen`) and point the hand-written union in `pcs-frontend/src/api/deliverables.ts:19` at that enum. This batch already fixed the runtime leak (the snapshot endpoint now emits the bare value), but the contract still records a bare `string`, so nothing in the drift check can catch a regression back to `DeliverableSignStatus.APPROVED` — the exact defect PE-1 was. Assumption: the deliverable side really has only these four states (`app/models/enums.py:124` confirmed).

findings.why_it_matters: 批准链现在是 submit 时冻结进 `approval_chain_snapshot` 的快照、中间步骤只读快照；但 approval-step 的 OpenAPI 描述（= 该端点 docstring，契约消费者唯一能看到的说明）仍写着「批准链来自项目绑定的 RECORD 矩阵」⇒ 读契约的人会以为中途重绑矩阵会改变待批角色，而实现恰恰相反（这正是本批修复的目的）。同一段描述还完全没提新增的失败路径：approval-step 现在每一步都比对提交人身份 ⇒ 提交人本人会吃到 403 APPROVAL_SELF_REVIEW_FORBIDDEN，而描述里只列了 APPROVAL_ROLE_MISMATCH ⇒ 消费方按描述建的错误映射会漏掉这一支。本批的前端注释已经改成「已提交记录的链由后端 approval_chain_snapshot 冻结」，前后端两侧对同一机制的表述已经分叉。
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the `approval_step` docstring (it is the only source of the OpenAPI description): state that the chain is frozen into `record.approval_chain_snapshot` at submit time, that intermediate steps read only that snapshot (rows without a snapshot fall back to the live matrix), and that every step re-compares the submitter's identity so the submitter gets 403 `APPROVAL_SELF_REVIEW_FORBIDDEN`. Add "提交时冻结批准链" to the `submit_approval` docstring and list the new error codes (422 `SIGNATURE_MATRIX_EMPTY_CHAIN`) in the error-code list. Then re-roll the contract: `pcs-backend/docs/openapi.json` + `pcs-frontend/openapi.snapshot.json` + `npm run api:gen` (the frontend's `src/types/api.d.ts` descriptions are generated and must be regenerated).

findings.why_it_matters: The approval chain is only frozen for records submitted after the snapshot column shipped. A record that is already IN_APPROVAL when the migration lands has approval_chain_snapshot = NULL, and both halves of the CWE-863 fix silently switch off for it: the per-step `submitted_by` re-assertion is skipped entirely (the `if snapshot and ...` guard is False), and `_next_approval_role` falls back to the LIVE project matrix. That restores the exact bypass the committee ruled to close — an approver who is also the submitter (or whose role is injected into a later step by a mid-flight matrix rebind) can approve their own record at step 2+, because the pending role is re-read from the live matrix and nothing compares it against the submitter. The same legacy rows also hit the fail-open role gate (`if record.approval_role and ...`), so a legacy row whose approval_role is NULL can be advanced by any PASS_CHECK role (CHECKER/REVIEWER/APPROVER/SYSTEM_ADMIN). New submissions are fully protected — the snapshot path is correct and the user_id comparison dominates the role comparison, so an actor with several roles cannot launder a later step. The gap is confined to rows created before the column existed, which is why this is P2 rather than P1.
findings.suggested_fix: Close the legacy path in `approval_step` instead of silently degrading it: when `record.approval_chain_snapshot` is None, (a) derive the submitter from the audit trail — the `audit_logs` row with action=RECORD_TRANSITION and `detail.transition == 'SUBMIT_FOR_CHECK'` for this resource, whose `user_id` is the submitting actor (`state_machine.py:477` writes `user_id=actor_user_id`, `state_machine.py:481` writes `"transition": transition.value`) — and raise 403 `APPROVAL_SELF_REVIEW_FORBIDDEN` if it equals `str(actor.user_id)`; (b) freeze the chain into `record.approval_chain_snapshot` on that first touch (matrix_id + steps + submitted_by + submitted_by_role) so every later step is snapshot-driven and a mid-flight rebind can no longer change the pending role. Assumption: legacy submissions went through the state machine (it is the only transition into IN_APPROVAL — `grep SUBMIT_FOR_CHECK app/` shows `records_actions.submit_approval` as the sole record-side caller), so a RECORD_TRANSITION/SUBMIT_FOR_CHECK audit row exists for the record.
